title: Why we should expect another Solheim Cup thriller
description: With no more than one point separating the teams at the past three Solheim Cups played in Europe there is every reason to expect that this week's contest will be just as exciting, writes Iain Carter.
fullText:
Recent history suggests this week's Solheim Cup will be another epic clash to follow hot on the heels of Great Britain and Ireland's dramatic victory over the United States in the Walker Cup.

The extraordinary climax at Lahinch last Sunday, where GB&I won with the last putt of the match, evoked memories of the past three Solheim Cups staged in Europe.

Three years ago in Spain the contest ended in a dramatic 14-14 tie to allow a delirious European team to hold on to the trophy, having initially wrestled it from American hands with a single-point victory at Gleneagles in 2019.

Then it was Suzann Pettersen's gut wrenching and ultimately successful putt on the final green at the Scottish course that decided the outcome.

And the previous Solheim Cup held on continental soil was a 2015 single point away win that capped an astonishing comeback by the United States in Germany.

So the past three matches in Europe have had no more than a point in them and the home team and the US are tied on aggregate at 42 points apiece.

"I think it just shows how important each game is," said British number one Lottie Woad, who makes her debut for Europe this week.

"Even if you're a couple down early, you can get it back and even just getting a half point could be vital. So I think you've just got to have that mentality that any half point or point helps."

Woad's compatriot and potential partner Charley Hull believes it can be tougher playing at home. "We get big crowds in both places, but obviously, it's a little more pressure over here when it's a home Solheim Cup," she said.

"You've just got to deal with it, just stay focused, and be in the zone."

Woad is among four rookies in the European team joining fellow Englishwoman Mimi Rhodes, France's Nastasia Nadaud and the big hitting Spaniard Julia Lopez Ramirez.

"I can't wait for them to tee it up," said European captain Anna Nordqvist. "It's always easy to try to describe to the rookies what it's like playing in the Solheim, but it's something that you need to experience.

"And you have to get your own feel for it. But I can't wait for them to feel what it's like stepping up on that first tee."

Players prepare for the intimidation of packed crowds in a huge grandstand around three sides of the opening tee, but of more significance will be the play as matches reach their climax down the closing stretch of holes.

And that will be amplified further if it is again close in the closing singles matches on Sunday. "Obviously it's elevated," said 2025 US Open winner Maja Stark.

"But you're still just playing golf and you're trying to do your best and you're trying to beat one person. There's not much more you can do.

"You can't rely on team-mates on Sunday afternoon. You have got to go back and remember what's important for me now."

The three-day contest starts on Friday with four foursomes - alternate shot - matches, with four fourball matches to follow. That format is replicated on Saturday before the 12 singles matches on Sunday.

American captain Angela Stanford is bullish about her line-up's ability to handle the unique pressure of the Solheim Cup. "I think they're very mentally tough," she said.

"They don't let things bother them. They let things kind of roll off their back if something doesn't go the way they planned and they seem really focused."

Ironically none of the 24 players are bringing stellar individual form into this match, not even Nelly Korda, the world number one who claimed her fourth title of the year by winning the US Women's Open in June.

Korda has had only two top-10s since that major triumph at the start of the summer and finished in a lowly share of 50th place at the recent FM Championship.

Since Korda's US Open victory there have been no LPGA wins for any of the Solheim players.

For Europe only Celine Boutier and Woad have claimed titles this season and American Lauren Coughlin is the sole other tour winner in 2026 on show.

But that backdrop will be forgotten when it comes to head-to-head matchplay. As the Walker Cup showed it goes to a rarified level when put into the team environment.

"You can lose or win any match regardless of rankings or how you're playing at the moment," said Linn Grant, Stark's Swedish compatriot who has missed the cut in five of her past six events.

"When everyone shows up on Friday, you're just going to bring your best game.

"It's so different playing matchplay in this setting. It's kind of like just everyone's best game just shows up normally which makes it a lot more fun to play as well."

Bernardus Golf Club, Netherlands

They are competing on a testing course at Bernardus Golf near Hertogenbosch in the Netherlands, which hosted the Dutch Open on the DP World Tour from 2021-23. It has a Surrey heathland feel, that can play like a seaside links in certain areas.

But that fast running aspect has been compromised by the storms that lashed the layout on Wednesday. "I think it's a great course for matchplay," said Stark.

"There are a lot of bunkers that you don't really want to be in. You can have a lot of really long irons into par-four holes as well."

The par threes are also likely to generate plenty of drama, especially the 15th where matches will reach a crucial stage. "It is my favourite hole both visually and strategically," says Bernardus club professional Roel Verdonschot.

"It is built for drama. Players must decide whether to take the risk and attack the pin for a short birdie opportunity or play towards the middle of the green and accept a longer putt.

"The tee is sheltered, so the wind can be difficult to feel, even though it is still influencing the shot."

And any match that goes the distance will involve an exceptionally tough 389-yard par-four closing hole. There is water from the left of the tee, while bunkers await players attempting to play safely towards the right.

And the green is tiny with a deep run-off to the left and water to the right. "The 18th is the most difficult playing hole at Bernardus," said Verdonschot.

"You face a tee shot that you cannot afford to miss left, but you do not want to miss right either. If a close match reaches the 18th, there is a very good chance of drama."

Which is completely in keeping with Solheim Cup matches, especially those staged in Europe.

title: Instagram boss says users will be ‘overwhelmed’ with brand content in algorithm-free world
description: Adam Mosseri says platform’s algorithm ‘feels like a black box’ but company trying to give users more control after Labor announces opt-out...
fullText:
Adam Mosseri says platform’s algorithm ‘feels like a black box’ but company trying to give users more control after Labor announces opt-out plan

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Instagram’s chief executive has said users will have a worse experience in an algorithm-free world, seeing more brand-related content, and spend less time on the app.

The comments come as the Australian government plans to give users the option to opt out of algorithms, with the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, announcing plans on Tuesday to require social media platforms to prompt users to choose between a feed of algorithm-recommended content or a reverse chronological feed of the pages users follow. Labor also plans to introduce a range of measures designed to address online harm on the sites.

In a briefing with journalists on Thursday to launch the company’s Algo Confessions series in Australia, Instagram’s chief executive, Adam Mosseri, did not comment directly on the Albanese government proposal but said Instagram had a range of algorithms in operation. Those include ranking which friends’ stories you see more often, or which users come up first in message suggestions based on interactions, as well as the algorithm that determines the content people see in their feeds.

The launch of the series in Australia is the first outside the US. It features celebrities and influencers detailing how Instagram determines what content ends up in a user’s feed, and how the user can have some control over that by adding or removing tags in their settings.

Mosseri said just a “very vocal minority” wants social media to go back to reverse chronological feeds, which he said would just incentivise people to post more.

“What ends up happening is the best way to get more reach is just to post more often and those who can afford to post the most often do and then therefore get the most reach,” he said.

“And it turns out your friends post a lot less than creators, who post a lot less than brands and companies.”

He said people would be “overwhelmed” with content from brands, and creators and friends would be drowned out.

“What happens is people become a bit less interested in the experience and they use it a lot less, which then means that there’s less reach to go around and people start to get more and more mad about the fact that their reach is going down because the overall pie gets smaller.”

He said engagement and user satisfaction goes down.

“It’s this interesting tension between what an individual might want and what happens when you actually explode that to the entire community,” he said.

“That’s not to say that ranking is perfect, it’s not, we make mistakes – one of the things that frustrates me about ranking is that we end up over-optimising for things that we can measure and undervaluing things that are more difficult to measure.”

Mosseri said Instagram’s ranking algorithm “feels like a black box” but was something Instagram was trying to give users more control over by opting out of certain topics in their recommendations.

He said in the future, Meta’s AI models could eventually allow users to talk to the app to understand why they are seeing certain types of content.

Mosseri said he did not believe the app to be the clinical definition of “addictive”.

“I don’t believe Instagram is addictive – I know that is controversial to say – I do think we often in English anyway conflate the way we colloquially use the word addicted … like ‘I’m addicted to this show and I’m binge watching it, which is not good for me’.”

He said clinically defined addictions have withdrawal symptoms, while social media does not have that effect, and “those things are different”.

Mosseri has made this claim before. Research has found some users can have an impulse to use a platform without being fully aware of it, and evidence shows frequent engagement with algorithms “alters dopamine pathways” that fosters dependency that is “analogous to substance addiction”.

In the landmark US court case centred on the addictive nature of Meta’s products, the company’s lawyer last month conceded to the court that it was “no dispute” people can struggle with social media, but the company has tools to address that. Meta later settled the case for US$18bn while denying any wrongdoing.

title: Pixel 11 Pro review: Google’s best pocket camera goes customisable
description:
Solid battery life, snappy performance and quality software make for a great smaller phone with a killer camera
Google’s latest Pro phone is out to prove it has the best camera on a smartphone while embracing customisation, allowing you to change the look and feel of your photos far beyond simple filters even if that means making them technically worse.
The Pixel 11 Pro packs the best of Google’s hardware and software into a still-pocketable and easy to handle frame, instantly making it a contender for best smaller phone of the year.
Screen: 6.3in 120Hz QHD+ OLED (495ppi)
Processor: Google Tensor G6
RAM: 12 or 16GB
Storage: 256, 512GB or 1TB
Operating system: Android 17
Camera: 50MP + 48MP UW + 48MP 5x tele; 42MP selfie
Connectivity: 5G, eSIM, wifi 7, UWB, NFC, Bluetooth 6, Thread and GNSS
Water resistance: IP68 (1.5m for 30 minutes)
Dimensions: 152.
fullText:
Solid battery life, snappy performance and quality software make for a great smaller phone with a killer camera

Google’s latest Pro phone is out to prove it has the best camera on a smartphone while embracing customisation, allowing you to change the look and feel of your photos far beyond simple filters even if that means making them technically worse.

The Pixel 11 Pro packs the best of Google’s hardware and software into a still-pocketable and easy to handle frame, instantly making it a contender for best smaller phone of the year.

Being smaller doesn’t make it cheap. The 11 Pro sits above the regular £879 Pixel 11 and costs from £1,079 (€1,199/$1,099/A$1,849) – £80 (€100/$100/A$150) more than last year, with double the storage but less memory owing to the cost of RAMageddon.

Little has changed on the outside for the Pro Pixels in several years. The new model is 0.1mm smaller in all directions and 3g lighter but has the same size 6.3in OLED screen, same polished aluminium and glass body and a large camera bar sticking out the back. It is an attractive design that has aged well.

The temperature sensor from previous Pixel Pro generations, which always felt like a gimmick, has been replaced by a coloured HiLight LED that works as a camera flash and notification light. The LED glows when you talk to Gemini or pulses with one of five colours when your favourite contact calls. But it doesn’t work for notifications of any other kind, so is a wasted opportunity.

The 11 Pro has the same Tensor G6 chip as the regular Pixel 11 and has 12 or 16GB of RAM depending on the storage version. It can’t match the raw performance of the top Qualcomm or Apple chips for games but is snappy in day-to-day tasks.

Battery life is just shy of two days with the screen actively used for about seven hours across a mix of wifi and 5G for browsing, messaging apps and photos. This is a bit behind the regular Pixel 11 but should see out even the heaviest of use days with some left in the tank. Most people will need to charge the 11 Pro every other day for general use.

Screen: 6.3in 120Hz QHD+ OLED (495ppi)

Camera: 50MP + 48MP UW + 48MP 5x tele; 42MP selfie

Connectivity: 5G, eSIM, wifi 7, UWB, NFC, Bluetooth 6, Thread and GNSS

Water resistance: IP68 (1.5m for 30 minutes)

Dimensions: 152.7 x 71.9 x 8.4mm

The 11 Pro runs the same Google version of Android 17 as the regular Pixel 11 and will be supported until August 2033 with operating system and security updates, making it one of the longest-lasting devices available.

It’s a polished experience with smooth animations, nice touches of haptic feedback across the system and enough customisation to make it yours. But as with other Pixel devices, the phone is a showcase for Google’s most advanced AI tools that are littered throughout the software.

The 11 Pro comes with six months of Google AI Pro subscription, which gives you access to Gemini Omni to generate surprisingly good eight-second videos, higher AI usage limits, 5TB of cloud storage and Google Health Premium.

But the most interesting tools are the local AI ones, including the new Rambler voice dictation feature in Gboard, which produces fully formed succinct sentences and paragraphs from your ramblings, removing unnecessary pauses, ums, ers and deviations. Gemini’s proactive assistance has also improved with more time-saving suggestions, although it only works in certain apps and not WhatsApp, Signal or other third-party apps.

The reason you buy a Pixel Pro is for the camera. The 11 Pro has a very good 42-megapixel selfie camera on the front and a similar winning triple camera system on the rear from last year: a 50MP wide, 48MP ultra wide and a 48MP 5x telephoto camera.

All three cameras capture really fantastic photos across a range of lighting conditions with very little effort. The wide and telephoto cameras now capture more light and slightly better detail, but the biggest boost is the new Instant Night Sight. It dramatically speeds up low-light photos by up to 4.5 times, which makes taking great shots in very dark scenes a lot easier.

The 5x telephoto camera manages a very good 10x crop zoom before stretching up to 120x magnification, first with a very good traditional digital zoom to 30x then using local generative AI to go beyond. The camera keeps the regular digital zoom image and the one processed by AI to add back lost detail, which can be remarkable or filled with artefacts.

Magic Capture takes video and photos automatically with just one button for point-and-shoot recording, which works well for events such as a birthday party.

But Camera Looks is the most interesting feature for getting creative with photography. It allows you to modify how the camera processes your photos, starting with subtle changes such as darker shadows and ranging to more distinctive looks such as “minimal”, which reduces the computational photography processing for a more raw photo. Other options include “digi”, which replicates the look of old digital cameras that have become popular, and “velvet”, which mimics the look of some film cameras. Each look can be further customised, allowing great creative licence.

The Pixel shoots great video with lots of stabilisation and processing tools including the new “Creator Suite”, which captures clips straight into a folder for storyboarding and trimming, with a teleprompter, framing for social media and speed enhancement.

The battery is rated to last in excess of 1,000 full-charge cycles with at least 80% of its original capacity. The phone is repairable by Google, third-party shops or self-repair with manuals and parts available.

The Pixel 11 Pro contains 31% recycled materials by weight. The company breaks down the phone’s environmental impact in its report and will recycle old devices for free.

The Google Pixel 11 Pro costs from £1,079 (€1,199/$1,099/A$1,849) in a choice of four colours.

For comparison, the Pixel 11 costs £879, Pixel 11 Pro XL costs £1,279, Pixel 11 Pro Fold costs from £1,799, the Pixel 10a costs £499, the Samsung Galaxy S26 costs £879, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra costs £1,279 and the Apple iPhone 17 Pro costs £1,099.

The Pixel 11 Pro is a refinement of multiple generations of Google’s Pro phones rather than an outright revolution, but that’s no bad thing.

It is one of the very best smaller phones, packing all the top-end hardware, cameras and AI features of Google’s most biggest and expensive model into a slightly cheaper and more pocketable form. You buy a Pro Pixel for the camera, which doesn’t disappoint with arguably the best photography on a phone at the moment.

The ability to customise the processing of your photos goes far beyond rivals for interesting creative potential. The dramatically faster Night Sight is also a significant improvement.

Gemini’s proactive tools show great potential but depend on using the right apps. The supercharged Rambler voice dictation system is fantastic, and there are many other little AI tools that are useful from time to time.

With just shy of two days battery life, a decent chip and quality software, the Pixel 11 Pro is a great pocketable phone. It just isn’t a massive upgrade on the already excellent Pixel 11 or recent Pixel Pro models.

Pros: great camera with extended zoom and extensive customisation, seven years of software updates, excellent screen, impressive dictation and local AI features, Qi2 wireless charging and magnetic accessory support, good battery life, great size, fast fingerprint and face recognition, six months of Google AI Pro included.

Cons: quite expensive, less memory on cheapest model than before, face unlock option not as secure as Face ID, raw performance and battery life short of best-in-class, no physical sim card slot in the US, not a massive upgrade.

Barry Melrose, Entertaining ESPN Hockey Analyst, Dies at 70
description: After 11 pro seasons as a rugged player, he led the L.A. Kings to the Stanley Cup Final in his first season as an NHL coach, then handled colorful commentary from 1994-2022.
fullText:
Barry Melrose, the blue-collar NHL defenseman who brought flash to the Los Angeles Kings as their coach and fun to ESPN during his nearly three decades as a colorful hockey analyst, has died. He was 70.

National Hockey League Commissioner Gary Bettman confirmed Melrose's death in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter. "From the flowing locks of his distinctive mullet to the flared lapels of his trademark long suit coats, Barry Melrose cut an unmistakable figure whenever you were fortunate enough to run into him at a rink or catch him on your television screen. You were even more fortunate if you engaged him in conversation or listened to his analysis, because he never failed to boost your love of the game of hockey," he wrote.

More from The Hollywood Reporter

Nina Shipman, Actress in 'The Oregon Trail' and 'The Munsters,' Dies at 88

Jim Geoghan, Co-Creator of 'The Suite Life of Zack & Cody,' Dies at 79

Bruce Davis, Longtime Film Academy Chief Executive, Dies at 83

Melrose's cause of death wasn't immediately available. In October 2023, he revealed that he had been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and was retiring.

"I've had over 50 extraordinary years playing, coaching and analyzing the world's greatest game, hockey," he said then in a statement. "It's now time to hang up my skates and focus on my health, my family, including my supportive wife, Cindy, and whatever comes next."

As a cigar-loving coach who sported a carefully groomed hairstyle (a mullet) and a closet full of $2,000 suits — a hockey version of the Los Angeles Lakers' Pat Reilly, if you will — Melrose took the Wayne Gretzky-led Kings to the precipice of their first Stanley Cup in 1993 in his first season guiding an NHL team.

Just 30 minutes after the Kings fired him in April 1995 near the end of his third season, Melrose was signed by ESPN to work as a studio analyst during the upcoming NHL playoffs. He called games part-time the next season before joining the network as a full-time analyst for the 1996-97 campaign.

"When [people] watch me on TV, I want them to go, 'Geez, I'd like to go for a beer with Barry Melrose and talk hockey. He seems like he'd be very interesting,'" he told the Los Angeles Times in 1995.

He left ESPN in June 2008 to coach the Tampa Bay Lightning, but that stint would last just five wins and 16 games before he got canned again. However, he was back on ESPN in 2009.

Melrose and Steve Levy reported from every Stanley Cup Final from 1994 until 2022. When Levy announced on the eve of the 2023 series that his ESPN colleague would not continue that streak, it led some to wonder if he were ill.

The third of four kids, Barry James Melrose was born on July 15, 1956, in Kelvington, Saskatchewan — a town of 900 people located 400 miles northwest of Winnipeg, Manitoba — and raised on a nearby farm. His father, James, built a rink on their property, and Melrose started skating when he could walk.

When he was 5, he took his first stick to the face and got a black eye. Later, he sold four pigs so he could buy his first pair of Tackaberry ice skates. His favorite NHL player was Tim Horton, a defenseman.

Melrose played three seasons of junior hockey with the Weyburn Red Wings and Kamloops Chiefs from 1973-76, then joined the Cincinnati Stingers of the World Hockey Association in 1976-77 after he was selected with the 37th pick in the WHA Draft. (He had been taken 36th by the Montreal Canadiens in that year's NHL Draft.)

After 178 games over three seasons with the Stingers, he appeared in 300 NHL games with the Winnipeg Jets, Toronto Maple Leafs and Detroit Red Wings through the 1985-86 season, collecting 10 goals and 23 assists to go with a whopping 728 penalty minutes. At 6-feet and 205 pounds, he was not afraid to mix it up.

He finished his playing career with the American Hockey League's Adirondack Red Wings in 1986-87, and guided the Medicine Hat Tigers to the Western Hockey League championship in 1988 in his first season as a coach.

He then led the WHL's Seattle Thunderbirds for one season and Adirondack for three more, with the Red Wings winning the Calder Cup in 1992, when he also served as the team's G.M.

The Kings, owned back then by the free-spending Bruce McNall, won a bidding war with the Detroit Red Wings, signing Melrose to a four-year contract in June 1992 to replace Tom Webster as their coach. The deal was worth a reported $1.3 million, believed to be the most ever paid for a first-time NHL coach to that point.

With Melrose behind the bench, the Kings, led by Wayne Gretzky, Luc Robitaille, Jari Kurri, Dave Taylor and Marty McSorley, edged the Maple Leafs on the road in Game 7 of the 1993 conference finals to advance to their first Stanley Cup Final.

"His idea of how the game should be played focused on speed — speed that would highlight the talents of the skilled players. I was in total agreement on that," Gretzky wrote in the foreword to Melrose's 2012 book, Dropping the Gloves: Inside the Fiercely Combative World of Professional Hockey.

"He and I had a meeting of the minds on day one. From then on, it was a pleasure playing for him. Sometimes it was an adventure, because Barry was always willing to try things."

Said Robitaille in the 2012 book A Season in Time, "If Barry had his way, you would never take a backward step."

The Kings would fall to the Canadiens in the Stanley Cup Final in five games, three of them in overtime, and miss the playoffs the next season. Melrose was then fired in April 1995 — three months after Gretzky was traded to the St. Louis Blues — with seven games left in the regular season and Los Angeles desperate to make the postseason (it didn't).

The Kings were also in a financial bind. "We used to eat at Spago," he told reporters, "and now we can't even get into a Sizzler." His record with L.A. was 79-101-29.

Nearly 13 years later, Melrose exited ESPN to go to Tampa to replace John Tortorella, who in 2004 had coached the Lightning to its first Stanley Cup.

"I think if I wouldn't have taken the job, I would have been a hypocrite," Melrose told The New York Times. "I'm sitting up there criticizing other people [at ESPN]. If you have a chance to get back in the fight and you don't take it, I would have been very disappointed with myself to not have the courage to do that."

But six weeks into the season, he was fired, and critics said he had lost touch with current strategies. Lucky for hockey fans, he would get a second shift on television.

In a video narrated by Gretzky, ESPN paid tribute to him after his retirement announcement.

Melrose was sworn in as a U.S. citizen in March 1998, and in 2004, he and Levy became part-owners of the now-defunct Adirondack Frostbite of the United Hockey League.

He played himself in the Russell Crowe-starring Mystery, Alaska (1999), on a 2001 episode of ABC's Spin City and in Slap Shot 2: Breaking the Ice (2002).

In addition to his wife — they first met when he was playing in Cincinnati and married eight months later in 1978 — survivors include their sons, Tyrell and Adrien.

In an undated interview, Melrose noted that you need drive in any endeavor to be a success. "It's gotta eat you up," he said. "You get out what you put in. If you put in nothing, then you will get nothing. If you put in tons, then you will get tons out."

title: BMW Signs Brad Binder To Factory WSBK Team
description: Brad Binder's next chapter starts on a production-based bike. BMW confirmed the South African will join its factory ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team for 2027. Binder had been a fixture of the Grand Prix paddock since 2012. He had been exclusively riding KTMs since 2015, including the last seven seasons in the premier class.
fullText:
Brad Binder's next chapter starts on a production-based bike. BMW confirmed the South African will join its factory ROKiT BMW Motorrad WorldSBK Team for 2027. Binder had been a fixture of the Grand Prix paddock since 2012. He had been exclusively riding KTMs since 2015, including the last seven seasons in the premier class.

Binder will line up alongside Miguel Oliveira, whose deal to stay with BMW for 2027 was confirmed last week, ahead of the French round at Magny-Cours. The pairing reunites two riders who already know each other's habits intimately, having shared a garage across Moto3, Moto2 and MotoGP during their KTM years. The two remain the only riders to have ever won a MotoGP race on a KTM.

With two riders signed for next season, Danilo Petrucci's run in the BMW WorldSBK project will end after the 2026 season. BMW says it is exploring ways to keep the Italian involved elsewhere. "At the same time, we would like to thank Danilo for his tremendous commitment," said Sven Blusch, head of BMW Motorrad Motorsport. "Together, we want to finish the current season strongly and are working towards a future together in other projects."

Binder arrives with a strong résumé and stalled form. The 2016 Moto3 World Champion took two MotoGP wins - Brno in 2020, the first premier-class victory for KTM, and the Red Bull Ring in 2021 - while adding nine podiums and Sprint wins in Argentina and Jerez in 2023. His best championship result came that same year, fourth overall. Since the start of 2024, though, he hasn't stood on a Grand Prix podium, his last being a second-place finish in Qatar. He currently sits 13th overall heading into this weekend's round at Misano.

Blusch made BMW's ambitions plain. "His goal is clear: he wants to fight for the World Championship title," he said, while acknowledging Binder faces a learning curve on the M 1000 RR. "First of all, he will need to get accustomed to the BMW M 1000 RR and to a new World Championship, and we are confident that he will do so quickly."

title: Aryna Sabalenka’s Reaction to Losing World No. 1 Ranking Goes Viral
description: ESPN captured Aryna Sabalenka’s candid reaction as Elena Rybakina ended her 99-week reign atop the WTA rankings. The post Aryna Sabalenka’s Reaction to Losing World No. 1 Ranking Goes Viral appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Aryna Sabalenka heard the roar before she saw what had happened.

The top-ranked player in women's tennis was practicing on Court P1 beside Arthur Ashe Stadium when the crowd erupted Wednesday afternoon. Sabalenka walked toward the televisions at the U.S. Open practice pavilion, leaned against a fence and watched Elena Rybakina complete the victory that ended her 99-week reign at No. 1.

ESPN captured Sabalenka viewing the final points of Rybakina's 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 quarterfinal victory over Zheng Qinwen.

There was no dramatic display. Sabalenka watched quietly, appeared to offer a small, knowing smile and then returned to work.

"Nothing she could do about it," ESPN analyst Chris Evert said during the broadcast.

It was a strikingly ordinary end to an extraordinary run.

Rybakina entered the quarterfinal needing one more victory to guarantee that she would pass Sabalenka when the WTA rankings update Monday.

Sabalenka could not influence the outcome. She had already secured her semifinal place by surviving Linda Noskova in three sets Tuesday. Even winning a third consecutive U.S. Open title would not provide enough points to remain No. 1.

Rybakina will have at least 8,681 ranking points Monday, while Sabalenka can finish with no more than 8,575, even if she successfully defends her championship.

Sabalenka stopped her practice session to watch Rybakina close out the match, then resumed preparing for Jessica Pegula.

The scene offered no evidence of anger, only recognition. Sabalenka understood exactly what Rybakina's final service hold meant.

Her uninterrupted reign, which began in October 2024, was over.

Rybakina overcame a slow, tense opening set against Zheng before taking control. She finished with 20 winners and earned the decisive break at 4-all in the third set when Zheng double-faulted.

The victory sent Rybakina into her first U.S. Open semifinal and made her the 30th woman to reach No. 1 since the WTA rankings began in 1975. She is also the first player representing Kazakhstan, male or female, to occupy the top ranking.

"It's just a number right now," Rybakina said afterward, emphasizing that she remained focused on winning the tournament.

The understated response mirrored Sabalenka's reaction from across the grounds. One player had reached the summit. The other had been displaced. Both still had matches to play.

Losing No. 1 does not eliminate Sabalenka's chance to leave New York with the trophy.

The four-time major champion will face Pegula in one semifinal, while Rybakina meets 2023 U.S. Open champion Coco Gauff in the other. A Sabalenka-Rybakina final would extend a rivalry that has already shaped the season.

Rybakina defeated Sabalenka in the Australian Open final to capture her second major title. Sabalenka responded by beating her at Indian Wells and Miami.

Now Rybakina has taken the ranking Sabalenka held for nearly two years.

The ESPN cameras preserved the precise moment Sabalenka absorbed that reality. She did not linger. She turned from the television and went back to practice, still chasing the only prize available in New York that could matter more.

title: The biggest NFL rule changes heading into the 2026 football season
description: (WFRV) — Every year, the NFL releases an updated playbook with newly worded and changed rules, much to the chagrin and controversy of avid football watchers. The nearly 100-page playbook includes four substantive rule changes from its current edition to last year’s, two of which involve kickoffs. The first rule change concerns kickoff formations. Rule […]
fullText:
(WFRV) -- Every year, the NFL releases an updated playbook with newly worded and changed rules, much to the chagrin and controversy of avid football watchers.

Popular Wisconsin zoo gives update on various lawsuits, legal battles

The nearly 100-page playbook includes four substantive rule changes from its current edition to last year's, two of which involve kickoffs.

The first rule change concerns kickoff formations. Rule 6-1-3 gives the receiving team more flexibility in designing return formations, so only five players must be on the restraining line when there are nine players in the setup zone. Previously, six were required. Now, only six are required if there are more than nine players.

The second rule change concerns kickoffs at the fifty-yard line. To prevent a situation where accepting a touchback off a 50-yard-line kickoff is worse than kicking it out of bounds, rule 6-1-5 makes it so that touchbacks from that kickoff placement are now placed at the 20-yard line, versus the 35-yard line like it used to be.

Still keeping with the kicking theme, the third rule drastically changes the concept of onside kicks. While only a trailing team could do onside kicks, Rule 6-1-6 now lets any team declare an onside kick at any point in the game.

The final drastic rule change concerns the power league officials have. Rule 19-2 allows league officials to intervene on a flagrant football or non-football act that wasn't called on the field. Previously, league officials could only help after a flagrant foul had already been called.

The rule states that the decision to intervene must be based on available video, and that the intervention must happen before the next play begins.

title: Raiders’ Michael Mayer Set for Major Role Change Without Brock Bowers
description: The Las Vegas Raiders were hit with a major blow with the injury to Brock Bowers, meaning there's a role shift for Michael Mayer. The post Raiders’ Michael Mayer Set for Major Role Change Without Brock Bowers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Ahead of the Week 1 clash with the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, the Las Vegas Raiders' biggest concern was the status of star running back Ashton Jeanty, who has been dealing with an ankle injury.

Unfortunately, a bigger issue has come to light for the storied NFL franchise, with superstar tight end Brock Bowers expected to miss the season opener and potentially Week 2 against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road at SoFi Stadium.

With Bowers on the mend for potentially two weeks or more, the Raiders will turn to veteran tight end Michael Mayer to pick up the slack, as he's expected to have an expanded role, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Raiders TE Michael Mayer already was going to be a part of the team’s attack – and his role now is expected to grow without Brock Bowers. https://t.co/HgYjdC3wln

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 9, 2026

"Raiders tight end Michael Mayer already was going to be a part of the team's attack, and his role now is expected to grow without Brock Bowers," Schefter wrote on his X account.

In the three years he's played for the Raiders, Mayer has had a limited role, which took a major hit when the team brought in Bowers, who quickly became one of the best tight ends in the NFL.

However, Mayer can be a formidable force on the field when getting the targets, which he'll certainly get now with Bowers on the shelf.

Over the course of three seasons in Las Vegas, Mayer has caught 83 passes for 788 receiving yards and three touchdowns.

It'll be interesting to see how much he's involved in new head coach Klint Kubiak's first game and whether the Notre Dame can help tilt the scales against the Dolphins in Week 1.

Obviously, losing Bowers for potentially a couple of games to start the season is not the way Kubiak wants to begin his stint with the Raiders.

Bowers is without a doubt the biggest receiving threat on the field for the Raiders, and the superstar tight end watching from the sideline is a big blow for Las Vegas, which is looking to get off to a quick start to the 2026 NFL season with a win against the visiting Dolphins.

According to Schefter, Bowers is confident he'll be back on the field for Las Vegas sooner rather than later.

"It sounds like Bowers is reasonably confident that he can be back in short order here. Maybe a game or two."@AdamSchefter with an update on Raiders' TE Brock Bowers 🏈 pic.twitter.com/V1HpdASvsy

— NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) September 9, 2026

"It sounds like Bowers is reasonably confident that he can be back in short order here," Schefter said. "Maybe a game or two."

One aspect of Bowers' absence that might actually be a positive for the Raiders is that it will require others in the passing game to step up and prove their worth right out of the gate against what could be a vulnerable Miami defense.

Kubiak will turn to Mayer at tight end, but it'll be interesting to see whether they'll get a big game from wide receivers like Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson.

The pressure is on the Raiders immediately, making for a compelling matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday in Las Vegas.

title: Robin Montgomery, Ashlyn Krueger, former US Open girls doubles champions, advance to 2026 women’s final
description: Five years after winning the 2021 US Open junior girls doubles title, Robin Montgomery and Ashlyn Krueger reunite and advance to the 2026 women's doubles final.
fullText:
Robin Montgomery and Ashlyn Krueger won the 2021 US Open girls doubles championship.

Five years later, the wildcard team reunited and is into the 2026 US Open women's doubles final. The duo will face the top seeded team of Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend.

Montgomery and Krueger were down 8-2 in the ten-point third-set match-deciding tiebreak to the second seeded team of Gabriela Dabrowski and Luisa Stefani before winning eight consecutive points to take it 10-8.

MORE: Elena Rybakina wins US Open quarterfinal, assumes WTA World No. 1 ranking from Aryna Sabalenka

They faced many accomplished and established doubles players en route to the final.

The team took on Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova and her Slovakian partner Rebecca Sramkova in the first round.

Aug 13, 2026; Mason, OH, USA; Ashlyn Krueger (USA) returns a shot against Lois Boisson (FRA) during the Cincinnati Open at Lindner Family Tennis Center. Mandatory Credit: Aaron Doster-Imagn Images

Montgomery and Krueger also had a big win over the ninth seeded team of Erin Routliffe and Aldila Sutjiadi.

Montgomery and Krueger will compete against Siniakova and Townsend in the 2026 US Open women's doubles final on Friday, September 11.

Whatever happens, tennis fans hope to see more of this young American team together in WTA tournaments throughout 2026 and especially at the Australian Open in 2027.

title: Charles Barkley Makes Unique Prediction For Lakers Season
description: The Los Angeles Lakers remain one of the top NBA stories after a polarizing offseason leads to mixed opinions. Some pundits believe the Lakers declined big time and will take a huge drop off this season. Others see the vision of a roster built for Luka Doncic that will experience strong success. Charles Barkley was […] The post Charles Barkley Makes Unique Prediction For Lakers Season appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers remain one of the top NBA stories after a polarizing offseason leads to mixed opinions. Some pundits believe the Lakers declined big time and will take a huge drop off this season. Others see the vision of a roster built for Luka Doncic that will experience strong success. Charles Barkley was down the middle and made a unique comment that appealed to both sides.

An appearance on the Bill Simmons Podcast saw Barkley sharing the following pros and cons to the Lakers:

"I really want to see the Lakers do well. First of all, I'm a big Luka fan, a big Austin Reaves fan. I think they're gonna be better than people realize. Luka and Kyrie took the Mavs to the Finals, come on, man. This team is probably better; this team is probably just as good as that team.

They're going to be fine, I think. Are they gonna win the championship? I don't think they're going to win the championship. But the league is better when the Boston Celtics, the Lakers, and the Knicks are good teams."

Barkley shared that he expects the Lakers to do a lot better than most pundits are predicting with a successful regular season. However, the good news ends there as Barkley also revealed he doesn't see the Lakers contending for a title due to the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder being far better.

One of the most interesting things about Barkley's quotes is that he believes this Lakers team is as good as the 2024 Dallas Mavericks squad that made the NBA Finals. Lakers GM Rob Pelinka had that in mind when building a similar roster to play to Luka's strengths.

However, a concern could be that Kyrie Irving was playing at a high level that Reaves will have to prove as the new Doncic lead co-star. Barkley expects the Lakers to easily make the top six playoff seeds and implied they could even have home court in the first round.

A lot needs to work in the Lakers favor, especially center Walker Kessler panning out to warrant getting paid big money and losing first round draft picks for him. New role players Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton must also step up to make up for the offense lost without LeBron James and others gone from last season.

The overall goal of contending for an NBA Championship remains hard to follow. San Antonio and Oklahoma City neutralize the Lakers' advantage of having Doncic since they also have superstars Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander.

Other West teams like the Minnesota Timberwolves and Denver Nuggets have higher ceilings due to their depth and previous success. The Lakers will need a dream season to give fans any hope of hanging another banner.

A smart move would be to play the season out and make big changes next summer if it becomes apparent this roster can't contend. Figuring out which talents fit with Luka will set the Lakers up for future success by getting rid of the others.

title: Lakers release new dazzling ‘specter’ jerseys
description: The Los Angeles Lakers will have a bold new look next season.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Lakers will have a bold new look next season.

During an event hosted by Nike, the Lakers revealed their new Specter jersey that they will wear a handful of times as an alternate jersey for the 2026-2027 NBA season.

The model walked out on the runway during the event and was seen wearing a No.77 Luka Dončić jersey that had a mixed colorway of purple and black going across it, while the color yellow was on the Lakers wordmark across the chest, and the outline on the numbers, and trim of the jersey.

There was also another unusual change to the jersey, as the Nike logo was seen placed across the middle of the chest, instead of its usual placement on the right shoulder.

On Wednesday, the NBA announced that they were issuing new Standard Issue Collection jerseys for every team in the NBA, as well as NBA Specter Edition uniforms as a way for teams to "trace their roots back to the earliest chapters of the league."

On top of having a mix of purple, yellow, and black, the jersey also features a blue and white stripe near the front shoulders, likely paying homage to the Lakers' old blue and yellow colors.

The Specter jersey is a bold choice by the NBA, which hasn't been shy to test the waters of creativity when it comes to creating different uniforms in the league.

"Basketball is more than a game — it's a culture and a form of self-expression," NBA VP Creative Director, Nike Basketball Ross Klein said. "This collection celebrates the attitude, creativity and individuality of today's hoopers, combining bold team identity and modern style so fans can show their connection to the game in their own way."

title: Neto hits 3-run HR over Green Monster as Angels beat Red Sox 6-4 to take series
description: Zach Neto hit a three-run homer over the Green Monster, Ryan Johnson gave up three runs over six innings and the Los Angeles Angels beat the Boston Red Sox 6-4 on Wednesday night to take the series.  Jose Siri added a two-run shot and Denzer Guzman a long solo homer for the Angels, who won consecutive games for the first time since taking three straight against Texas on Aug. 11-13.  Winning for just the fourth time in 15 games, Los Angeles captured its first road series since taking two of three from Houston on Aug. 18-20.
fullText:
BOSTON (AP) — Zach Neto hit a three-run homer over the Green Monster, Ryan Johnson gave up three runs over six innings and the Los Angeles Angels beat the Boston Red Sox 6-4 on Wednesday night to take the series.

Jose Siri added a two-run shot and Denzer Guzman a long solo homer for the Angels, who won consecutive games for the first time since taking three straight against Texas on Aug. 11-13.

Winning for just the fourth time in 15 games, Los Angeles captured its first road series since taking two of three from Houston on Aug. 18-20.

Roman Anthony hit a two-run homer and Wilyer Abreu a solo one for Boston, which lost the final two games after winning the opener Monday.

Coming in with a 1.67 ERA in his last six starts when he gave zero or one run five times, Johnson (4-8) breezed through his four scoreless innings, giving up two singles while his teammates built a 6-0 lead.

Jake Bennett (9-7) gave up a season-high six runs — five coming in one inning to surpass his previous high of four — on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings.

Ben Joyce got the final three outs for his fourth save despite giving up a run.

The Angels halted Boston's five-game winning streak Tuesday.

Neto hit his 25th of the season into the first row of Monster seats to make it 3-0. After Mike Trout doubled, Siri sent his eighth in Boston's bullpen.

Guzman's caromed off a billboard high above the Monster seats.

Behind a three-game sweep in Anaheim in early July, Boston took the season series, 4-2.

Angels: LHP Yusei Kikuchi (1-5, 4.96 ERA) is set to start the opener of a three-game series Friday against the Nationals.

Red Sox: RHP Sonny Gray (17-4, 2.69) looks to continue his strong season in the first of three against the Royals on Friday.

title: Notre Dame football cornerback DJ McKinney reflects on 'amazing' debut
description: Notre Dame football's DJ McKinney ended up playing 43 defensive snaps in the opener, highlighted by a pick-six.
fullText:
SOUTH BEND — DJ McKinney's Notre Dame football debut saw him find the end zone on a 55-yard interception return to key the second-half surge against Wisconsin.

How's that for a Colorado transfer announcing his arrival?

"Man, it's amazing," the fifth-year cornerback said after practice on Wednesday Sept. 9. "Amazing feeling, especially doing it in front of our fans and everything. It's different from in practice."

Even though Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph threw the ball directly to McKinney as if it were a practice drill?

"I made them pay for it," McKinney said with a grin.

After singing the Alma Mater, he joined dozens of his new teammates in a Lambeau Leap into the student section in Green Bay.

"That was fun," he said. "We all talked about it before when we knew we were going to play at Lambeau Field. I'm not a Packers fan. I don't really watch them, but I was told that's what they do. And I was like, 'Oh, that's cool. Maybe once we win, we can do that.'"

The Texan from Colleyville, just west of the Dallas-Fort Worth airport, said he "definitely would have" done the Lambeau Leap on his pick-six if not for all the red on that end of the field.

"That was the Wisconsin side," he said. "I didn't want to risk anything."

More: It took a half, but we saw the real Notre Dame football against Wisconsin

McKinney ended up playing 43 defensive snaps in the opener, second only to Leonard Moore among Irish cornerbacks. Michigan transfer Jayden Sanders rotated in for a couple of series in the first half, but when Sanders gave up a 28-yard touchdown to Malachi Coleman, the Irish went with McKinney the rest of the way.

All is forgiven, it seems, between McKinney and his new position coach, Aaron Henry.

Before McKinney, 22, made the switch from Oklahoma State to Deion Sanders' Colorado in January 2024, he was texting with Henry, then running the Illinois defense.

"I still have his text thread," Henry said during training camp. "I said, 'Dude, you left me on read!' And I show him it all the time. He just starts laughing."

The kicker, Henry said, is that he's from Immokalee in southwest Florida, not far from Sanders' roots in North Fort Myers.

"I said, 'You left me for Coach Prime! You left me for a Hall of Famer, dude!'" Henry said in August. "(McKinney) made a pretty good decision. But I'm giving him a hard time about that."

Asked about ghosting Henry two stops ago, McKinney pleaded ignorance.

"I never saw his message," the player said. "I think that's what he thought I did. I don't remember seeing his message."

Henry is having no trouble delivering his messages to McKinney now.

"It's amazing," McKinney said. "I've learned a lot since I've been here, and it's my fifth year. You can learn something each day and just continue to build."

After wearing No. 8 at his previous stops, McKinney opted for No. 2 with the Irish. That just so happens to be the same number Sanders wore at Florida State 40 years ago.

It was Sanders, after McKinney ended his 2024 season with three picks in four games, who suggested publicly his latest cornerback prodigy had everything it takes to be an eventual NFL first-round pick.

"Man, it meant a lot, especially coming from Coach Prime, one of the greatest at his position to do the job," McKinney said. "It certainly built my confidence."

After recording his second career pick-6 in the prime-time win over Wisconsin, McKinney didn't receive a congratulatory text from Sanders, but he's pretty sure his old coach was aware.

"I feel like he's always just watching, making sure that he stays in contact," McKinney said. "He's always there if I need him, you know?"

Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

title: NFL Kickoff 2026: Patriots lead Seahawks 7-0 at halftime
description: The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.
fullText:
The Patriots lead the Seahawks 7-0 at halftime, but Seattle has a bigger concern moving forward.

Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold exited the game after the first series with a hip injury. He appeared to suffer it when he was sacked by Dre'Mont Jones on third down, which brought up a punt.

Darnold limped to the sideline before he was eventually examined in the medical tent. He then limped off the field up to the locker room for further evaluation.

Just before halftime, the Seahawks ruled him out.

Backup Drew Lock played the rest of the first half for Seattle. So far, he's completed 6-of-8 passes for 51 yards. But the Seahawks have also struggled to move the ball, registering six first downs.

On the other side, Drake Maye has been a lot more effective than he was against Seattle's defense in Super Bowl LX back in February. He's gotten off some quick passes and used his legs effectively to scramble. Though Maye's most productive pass was one that wasn't even completed — as newcomer A.J. Brown drew a defensive pass interference penalty that put the Patriots at Seattle's 2-yard line.

On the next play, Maye tossed a 2-yard touchdown to rookie tight end Eli Rairdon for the NFL's first touchdown of 2026.

Maye finished the first half 10-of-12 for 66 yards with a touchdown.

The Patriots have 10 first downs, 130 yards, and are 3-of-7 on third down.

Seattle has 120 yards and is 1-of-6 on third down. They may want to have a heavy dose of rookie Jadarian Price in the second half, who has 42 yards on his six carries in his debut.

The Patriots will receive the second-half kickoff.

title: What happened to Sam Darnold? Why Drew Lock took over as Seahawks QB early in season opener
description: Here's what happened to Darnold in the first quarter and why he didn't play most of Wednesday's game.
fullText:
What happened to Sam Darnold? Why Drew Lock took over as Seahawks QB early in season opener originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl title defense got off to an inauspicious start as they lost their starting quarterback on their first drive.

Sam Darnold was forced to leave the contest early in the first quarter after a sack appeared to cause a right leg injury. Darnold has been fairly healthy in the past two years, starting 34 combined games for the Seahawks and Minnesota Vikings, but did have injury issues to begin his NFL career.

Darnold's health will continue to be a Week 1 storyline, as he was later ruled out by Seattle — it could prove to be challenge for the Seahawks that they never faced during their magical 2025 season. However, Seattle did roll out a veteran quarterback as a backup.

LIVE: Patriots vs. Seahawks updates, highlights from NFL season opener

Here's what happened to Darnold in the first quarter.

Darnold suffered a hip injury on the Seahawks' first drive of the game, which ended in a Patriots sack on 3rd-and-6. Patriots defensive tackle Dre'Mont Jones chased Darnold down and sacked the quarterback, but he landed on Darnold's right leg in the process.

Darnold limped off the field and initially tried to wave away the medical staff, but he ended up in the blue tent anyway. Then, the medical staff took Darnold to the locker room for further evaluation, as the quarterback had a prominent limp.

Kaylee Hartung gives an update on the status of Sam Darnold.

📺 NFL Kickoff on NBC & Peacock pic.twitter.com/CGG2F8TT4b

Darnold will not return to Wednesday's game, ruled out by the Seahawks before halftime.

The Seahawks initially ruled Darnold as questionable to return to the game with a hip injury as he continued to get evaluated in the locker room. Considering it is Week 1, and that the Seahawks have 11 days until they play next, the team will likely be cautious with their starting quarterback.

.@Seahawks injury update: QB Sam Darnold is Questionable (hip).

NFL Week 1 picks against the spread

Darnold has been the Seahawks' starting quarterback since the start of the 2025 season, when he helped lead the team to a Super Bowl championship. Now entering his second season as a starter, Darnold is cemented in that spot thanks to his play throughout last year.

Behind Darnold is Drew Lock, a veteran quarterback in his second stint with the Seahawks. Lock first joined Seattle as part of the Russell Wilson trade with the Denver Broncos, and he started two games and played in four during the 2023 season. After a stop with the New York Giants, Lock returned to Seattle last year, where he played in five games as Darnold's backup.

The Seahawks' third-string quarterback is Jalen Milroe, the former Alabama quarterback whom Seattle drafted in the third round in 2025. Milroe appeared in three games for the Seahawks as a rookie, where he worked primarily as a wildcat quarterback.

title: Patriots vs. Seahawks live updates: Score, news, discussion from Week 1
description: The Patriots will open their 2026 regular season on Wednesday night.
fullText:
Coming off a loss in Super Bowl LX, the New England Patriots spent their offseason overhauling a roster that led them to a conference title but that ultimately over-performed in 2025. So, in order to establish themselves as a true powerhouse in the league rather than a one-hit wonder, Mike Vrabel and company invested serious resources — from high-profile free agency signings, to draft investments, to one of the biggest trades in recent franchise history.

Training camp and to a lesser degree preseason already allowed for some first insight into the new-look Patriots' progress in Year 2 under Vrabel. However, the overall stakes were still relatively minimal throughout the summer.

On Wednesday night, all of that changes. In a rematch of said Super Bowl, the Patriots will take on the Seattle Seahawks to kickstart the 2026 NFL regular season.

Wednesday, Sept. 9, 8:20 p.m. ET | Lumen Field, Seattle, WA | Broadcast information | Inactives | Game day roster

Starting the game on defense after winning the coin toss, the Patriots surrendered back-to-back first downs to open the game. However, aided by a subsequent false start penalty against the Seahawks, the unit eventually got off the field thanks to a Dre'Mont Jones sack on third down — a play that forced Seattle quarterback Sam Darnold to take a trip to the blue medical tent.

The Patriots offense opened deep in its own territory, but a 10-yard Drake Maye scramble gave the unit some breathing room and moved the chains for a first time. It would have remained New England's only first down of the series if not for a late hit on Maye following another rushing attempt on a 3rd-and-5. The team was unable to capitalize on the Seattle error, however, and was forced to punt after Maye was pressured into throwing incomplete on the next third down.

The next drive saw a change at quarterback for the Seahawks. With Darnold heading to the locker room due to a hip injury he sustained on the opening series, backup Drew Lock entered the contest. Seattle's offense did manage one first down on Lock's first possession, but stalled when Christian Elliss met running back George Holani in the hole and short of the line to gain on a 3rd-and-2 rushing attempt.

New England's second offensive series saw Drake Maye's first pass completions of the night to Mack Hollins and A.J. Brown, respectively. However, the momentum built by those plays was not sustained and the Patriots eventually had to punt after Rhamondre Stevenson was tackled for a loss on a 3rd-and-1 carry.

The defensive battle continued into the second quarter. Seattle gained one first down on its third drive, but had to punt the ball away after a Drew Lock throw on third down came close to being picked off by Christian Gonzalez.

Their third drive was one of multiple firsts for the Patriots. They converted their first third downs of the game on throws to DeMario Douglas and A.J. Brown, and they moved into Seattle territory for the first time on the day. Most importantly, they scored their first points: after a pass interference penalty drawn by Brown on a flea-flicker, Maye hit a wide-open Eli Raridon for a touchdown. | Patriots 7, Seahawks 0

First NFL catch, first NFL TD @EliRaridon!!

📺 NBC pic.twitter.com/M9ZmApdGAt

The Patriots' rookies began leaving their mark in the second quarter. After the Eli Raridon touchdown on the previous drive, fellow draft pick Gabe Jacas registered his first career sack the next series: he took down Drew Lock on a second-effort play for a loss of 7 yards. Seattle nearly dug itself out of a 3rd-and-22 hole thanks to a 21-yard pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but an offsides penalty on the ensuing 4th-and-1 prompted yet another. Seahawks punt.

The Patriots continued to find some offensive success on their first drive after the Raridon touchdown, but they were unable to sustain it. Despite returning into Seahawks territory thanks to a third-down conversion to A.J. Brown and another Drake Maye scramble, the series eventually ended in Mitch Wishnowsky's third punt of the night.

Seattle didn't do anything with the ensuing possession to close out the first half.

title: Red Sox drop series behind timely Angels home runs
description: The Red Sox haven’t been super sharp in September, though they haven’t exactly needed to be. There shouldn’t be a ton of panic after the Angels took two of three in Boston with the 6-4 loss for the Red Sox in the rubber match. The magic number will fall. The team will be whole soon. […]
fullText:
The Red Sox haven't been super sharp in September, though they haven't exactly needed to be. There shouldn't be a ton of panic after the Angels took two of three in Boston with the 6-4 loss for the Red Sox in the rubber match.

The magic number will fall. The team will be whole soon. So don't freak out about a series loss to a lowly Los Angeles team.

Here's three takeaways from Wednesday night's loss

Jake Bennett struggled with one tough inning where the home run ball. Los Angeles scored five runs off the lefty in the third inning from a three-run blast from Zach Neto, who also had four hits Tuesday night, and a two-run shot for Jose Siri.

The Angels added another run in the fourth inning and didn't look back behind another solid start from Ryan Johnson, though the Red Sox did snap his six-start streak of allowing two runs or fewer as he surrendered three earned runs.

RELAX, JUST GET THE LINEUP HEALTHY 
Boston showed some solid fight late with four runs coming as the game went on. Roman Anthony and Wilyer Abreu impressed as they both slugged homers over 400 feet.

While the group had ups and downs in the series, Willson Contreras could rejoin the team this weekend after a Friday rehab assignment with Double-A Portland. Ceddanne Rafaela appears on the right track after a retroactive injured list designation as well.

As we've discussed all September, just get the lineup healthy for the postseason. They will.

The loss would have kept the magic number for the Red Sox at 10 to clinch an American League playoff spot.

Instead, Boston got some help from an American League East rival as the Blue Jays lost 2-0 to the Athletics already Wednesday. That Toronto defeat dropped Boston's magic number to nine with 15 games remaining.

title: Terence Crawford hints at return, calls out Boots Ennis
description: Terence Crawford may rescind his retirement to fight Boots Ennis.
fullText:
Terence Crawford has hinted at a potential return to boxing with a 'Boots' Ennis callout.

'Bud' is one of the very few combat sports athletes who bowed out while on top. Many consider his career-defining win against Canelo Alvarez enough to label him the greatest boxer of his generation. We are approaching the one-year mark since Crawford's retirement, but it seems he is getting the itch to return.

The demand for a Terence Crawford vs. Jaron 'Boots' Ennis clash spiraled out of control after the two went at each other live on DAZN earlier this month. During the live segment, Ennis continued his long-standing claim that he would make easy work of Crawford if they ever met in the ring. A back-and-forth commenced between the two, with neither side backing down. The visuals sparked debate online, but it began losing steam when it looked like the fight would never happen.

Just days later, a bout between the two now looks closer than ever.

In a post on social media earlier today, Terence Crawford hinted at a potential call-out of Boots Ennis. Folding to the fans' demands, Crawford issued a challenge to Ennis: If I come out of retirement, would you fight me next?

"I wanna see something!" Crawford said on X. "Y'all wanna see me come back and fight so bad, don't y'all? Jaron Ennis, would you fight me next if I come outta retirement?"

I wanna see something! Yall wanna see me come back and fight so bad don’t yall? @JaronEnnis would you fight me next if I come outta retirement?

A fight between the two undefeated boxers would feel reminiscent of boxing during its glory days. Real stakes on the line. And Ennis was interested in the idea, simply replying:

@terencecrawford 1000% ! https://t.co/lWVCxMJAkm

Rumors claim Crawford could be tempted to return. A huge payday and glory await, though Ennis would allegedly need to become the undisputed champion before any serious fight talks get underway.

title: Schwarber hits grand slam for 44th homer in Phillies' 11-7 win over Astros
description: Kyle Schwarber hit a grand slam for his majors-leading 44th home run, Trea Turner also homered and the Philadelphia Phillies overcame two deficits to beat the Houston Astros 11-7 on Wednesday night.  The Phillies’ offense masked a shaky performance from starter Cristopher Sanchez (17-5), who got his NL-leading victory despite allowing six runs on 10 hits in six innings.  Schwarber connected on a 3-2 sweeper from reliever A.J. Blubaugh to cap a six-run sixth inning.
fullText:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Kyle Schwarber hit a grand slam for his majors-leading 44th home run, Trea Turner also homered and the Philadelphia Phillies overcame two deficits to beat the Houston Astros 11-7 on Wednesday night.

The Phillies' offense masked a shaky performance from starter Cristopher Sanchez (17-5), who got his NL-leading victory despite allowing six runs on 10 hits in six innings.

Schwarber connected on a 3-2 sweeper from reliever A.J. Blubaugh to cap a six-run sixth inning. It was Schwarber's 10th career grand slam and his fourth home run in the last five games.

Turner had a pair of hits, including a solo homer, off of Astros starter Hunter Brown. Turner also had a single and stole a base to get into scoring position before scoring on a two-run single by Bryce Harper in the third, an inning in which the Phillies erased an early 4-0 deficit by scoring four of their own.

Luis Arraez, Edmundo Sosa and Bryan De La Cruz also had RBIs for Philadelphia.

Isaac Paredes and Cam Smith each hit two-run homers for Houston, and Yordan Alvarez had an RBI double.

LHP Bryan King (2-5) took the loss in relief for Houston. He didn't record an out and allowed four runs, three earned, on three hits.

Jose Altuve became just the second Astros player to record 2,500 career hits when he doubled off Sanchez in the third. He joined Craig Biggio, who is Houston's all-time hit leader (3,060). Altuve and Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman are the only active players with at least 2,500.

Astros RHP Cristian Javier (2-5, 5.98) was set to start the series finale against Philadelphia's Zack Wheeler (12-5, 3.23) on Thursday.

title: Barry Melrose, longtime ESPN analyst former Cincinnati Stingers player, dies
description: Barry Melrose, was a longtime ESPN analyst before his Parkinson's disease diagnosis. He joined the Cincinnati Stingers of the World Hockey Association in the 1976-77 season.
fullText:
Barry Melrose, the former NHL coach who starred as an ESPN hockey analyst, has died at age 70, the network reported.

Melrose had retired from his broadcasting duties in 2023 after being diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

"I've had over 50 extraordinary years playing, coaching and analyzing the world's greatest game, hockey. It's now time to hang up my skates and focus on my health, my family, including my supportive wife Cindy, and whatever comes next," Melrose said in a statement at the time.

"I'm beyond grateful for my hockey career, and to have called ESPN home for almost 30 years. Thanks for the incredible memories and I'll now be cheering for you from the stands."

Melrose, a defenseman, played in the NHL and World Hockey Association and went into coaching after his retirement.

Melrose joined the Cincinnati Stingers of the World Hockey Association for the 1976-77 season, and played for them until the league ceased operations after the 1978-79 season.

His 178 games played ranks eighth in Stingers' history. His 343 penalties minutes is second in club history, including a single-season record of 222 in 1978-79.

After stints in the Western Hockey League and American Hockey League, he began coaching the Los Angeles Kings in 1992 and took the Wayne Gretzky-led team to the Stanley Cup Final in his first season. The Kings lost to the Montreal Canadiens in five games in that series.

He coached the Kings for another two seasons and was fired in the third season. He also briefly coached the Tampa Bay Lightning in 2008-09.

Between the coaching stints, he was a popular ESPN studio analyst noted for his observations and his trademark mullet.

"Barry was my best friend at ESPN," John Buccigross posted on X. "A big brother figure of rock solid values. I am shook to my core. Barry gave his life to hockey and some of his ESPN family, like me, learned of his shocking death today while at a hockey rink in Las Vegas preparing for the upcoming season. Chilling and fitting--the rink was Barry's home. A more beloved ESPN institution there has not been. We love you, Barry. Forever."

title: Barry Melrose, Longtime ESPN Hockey Analyst, Dies at 70
description: Barry Melrose, a former NHL player and coach who later served as a hockey analyst at ESPN for 27 years, died on Wednesday following a battle with Parkinson's disease. He was 70.
fullText:
Barry Melrose, a former NHL player and coach who later served as a hockey analyst at ESPN for 27 years, died on Wednesday following a battle with Parkinson's disease. He was 70.

Melrose's wife, Cindy, confirmed his passing to his longtime employer, with ESPN sharing a statement on his death Wednesday evening.

"For decades, Barry Melrose was one of the most distinctive and trusted voices in hockey," the sports broadcasting network shared in a statement. "His knowledge of the game was deep, his candor was refreshing and his passion was unmistakable. He was a foundational part of ESPN's hockey coverage, and fans and teammates truly appreciated his entertaining delivery and charismatic personality."

The company's statement added: "We send our deepest condolences to his loved ones. He always kept it interesting and he will be missed."

More to come…
